orders.title: WO-012 — Register starter v0.87.0: name DotLn-Angular's releases `DotLn Angular`, keep the base checkout's output at close, declare the operator's commit identity and verify the instance
orders.objective:
after this order merges, `dotln.config.json` declares for
`dotln-angular` a target release policy with the display name
`DotLn Angular`, so a target order that carries a
`Target release classification` header closes with an annotated tag and a
GitHub Release titled `DotLn Angular <tag>` (the first is
`DotLn Angular v0.1.0`), and `release.close` is in the registration's allowed
effects; the clone's base checkout keeps its output at every target close
under `baseDisposablePolicy: "judge-only"` while the close still judges it
and refuses undeclared ignored material; `contributions.operatorAuthor`
names the author identity of this repository's session commits, so the kit's
publish helper passes its sign-off rule for the operator's own commits; no
historical order is declared, because WO-001 is a closed order under
control; the kit's two gates pass at v0.87.0 on this instance's records, with
any stale generated artifact repaired by `npm run sync`; and the repository
profile and WS-001 state the policy, the node-spelled publish helper the next
target order's draft must use, and what the close keeps.

**Observed gap (dated 2026-10-20, main at `d109e22`, update pull request
#14 open):** `dotln.config.json` declares no `release` key
under the registration, keeps `release.close` in `deniedEffects`, declares no
`baseDisposablePolicy` and no `contributions`. At v0.87.0
`validateRepositoryRelease` admits `displayName` with the launchpad's
validator and 64-character limit (the planning pass validated the exact
bytes of the Design with `validateConfig` in a scratch copy: admitted, and a
65-character name refused); the close reads `baseDisposablePolicy` and
defaults it to `delete`; and `worktree publish` runs
`contributionSignoffRules` over `origin/main..HEAD` before any push and fails
each commit whose author is not the declared `operatorAuthor` and carries no
matching `Signed-off-by` trailer. No commit on `main` carries such a trailer
and every session commit is authored as the operator, so this order's own
final publish would fail without the declaration. Without the display name,
DotLn-Angular's first target Release would be titled `dotln-angular v0.1.0`;
under the default policy, WO-005's close on 2026-10-20 deleted `.nx` (119
files), `dist` (10) and `node_modules` (37,877) in the target worktree and
found nothing to delete in the base checkout, which held no ignored file. The
profile and WS-001 still say the kit cannot name a target release.
orders.cost:
adds to `dotln.config.json` one `release` object and one
`baseDisposablePolicy` key on the `dotln-angular` registration and one
top-level `contributions` object (about 300 bytes), moves `release.close`
from the registration's denied effects to its allowed effects, rewrites the
profile's `## Release close` section, adds WS-001's member and delivery-state
rows and this order's evidence. Removes nothing tracked beyond the moved
effect. Wall-clock: about 30 to 60 minutes of executor work plus the fixed
cycle (activation, verification, final review, release close); unknown until
run. Context bytes: the 2026-10-20 planning document §4, §6 and §7, core's
v0.87.0 release notes §Read before upgrading (WO-218), `scripts/lib/config.mjs`
(`validateRepositoryRelease`, `validateRepositories`, `validateContributions`,
`validateHistoricalWorkOrders`), `scripts/lib/contributions.mjs`,
`scripts/worktree.mjs` §publish, `scripts/lib/target-worktree-close.mjs`,
this order, about 80 KB. Commands added: none. Tokens: unknown until run.
Steps: 9. Re-mints: none; no registered evidence source, feedback source or
machinery suite source is edited, so `npm test` is the product gate.

orders.title: WO-006 — The component taxonomy made real in DotLn-Angular: `ui` with fragments, templates, wrappers over the operator-confirmed vendor and shared composites, the lint rules that enforce the roles by location, the `dotln` shell layout, and the `home` feature with its composites, layout, mapper, container and facade behind a lazy route, with accessibility checks in e2e
orders.objective:
a developer opening any component in DotLn-Angular can tell
from its directory what it is allowed to know, lint refuses the violations the
taxonomy's rules name, the `dotln` shell renders through a layout library with
content projection, and the `home` feature demonstrates every kind once:
fragments and templates in `ui`, wrappers over the vendor, a composite, a
layout, a mapper over a discriminated view-model union, a container reading
one `vm` signal from `HomeFacade`, behind a lazy route built from `BasePaths`.

about 60 source files and the taxonomy documents. Removes the WO-004
placeholder page. Wall-clock: about 6 to 8 hours of executor work plus the
fixed cycle; unknown until run. Context bytes: WS-001 §Design, the foundation
documents, the vendor's component API for the four wrapped components, this
order, about 120 KB. Commands added in the target: none (`lint:fixtures`
gains cases). Tokens: unknown until run. Steps: 14. Re-mints: none.

orders.title: WO-007 — Events, stores and data access for DotLn-Angular: the tiered event groups in `events`, NgRx SignalStore with the Events plugin, call state and the trinity through `data-access`, `HomeStore` behind `HomeFacade`, the app-tier stores for feature flags, navigation with canonical routes and errors in `state`, HTTP interceptors for base URL, timeouts and errors, MSW in development and in tests, and the action-hygiene check
orders.objective:
state in DotLn-Angular flows one way through typed events:
UI events dispatched by containers through facades, data-access events as
reusable commands with call state, navigation events resolved by one store
through canonical routes, app events for flags and errors; every event is
declared in `@dotln-angular/events` under its tier, the hygiene check counts
the exceptions, `HomeStore` loads tiles through HTTP answered by MSW in
development and in tests, and the shell shows the error store's state.

`libs/shared/state`, `libs/features/home-data-access`, the MSW worker and
handlers, the interceptors, the hygiene check script, about 70 source files;
adds `@ngrx/signals`, `@angular-architects/ngrx-toolkit` (or a house
`withCallState`), `msw` pinned to 3.x (`~3.0.3` or the current 3.x at
activation, recorded) to the workspace. Removes `HomeFacade`'s static data.
Wall-clock: about 6 to 8 hours of executor work plus the fixed cycle; unknown
until run. Context bytes: WS-001 house rules 8, 11, 16, the NgRx Events plugin
and toolkit declarations, the MSW browser and Node guides, this order, about
150 KB. Commands added in the target: `npm run lint:hygiene`, `npm run msw:init`.

orders.title: WO-008 — Authentication and permissions for DotLn-Angular, legitimate from the Angular side: `auth` with an OpenID Connect authorization-code-with-PKCE client behind a port, in-memory token handling with single-flight refresh, expiry and invalid-token paths, the auth and permission stores, route and feature permission checks from a declared adjacency list, the mocked identity provider through MSW, and the failure-case matrix in unit and e2e tests
orders.objective:
a visitor to `apps/dotln` signs in through an OpenID Connect
authorization-code flow with PKCE against a mocked provider, holds tokens only
in memory, is refreshed once when a request meets an expired token and
signed out when refresh fails or a token is invalid, sees only the routes and
features the declared permission model grants, and every failure case in the
matrix below has a passing test; swapping the mocked provider for a real one
changes configuration and nothing in the Angular code.
orders.cost:
adds `libs/shared/auth` with its kit, the mocked identity provider
handlers and signing key for development, the `authHttpEvents` and
`sessionEvents` groups, guards, the permission directive, the `/login` and
`/denied` routes, about 60 source files; adds one OpenID Connect client
library and `jose` (development signing in the mock) to the workspace.
Removes nothing. Wall-clock: about 8 to 12 hours of executor work plus the
fixed cycle; unknown until run. Context bytes: WS-001 house rule 17, the
events and state documents, the client library's documentation, this order,
about 160 KB. Commands added in the target: none. Tokens: unknown until run.
Steps: 15. Re-mints: none.

criteria.text:
`grep -rlE "localStorage|sessionStorage" libs/shared/auth/src apps/dotln/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v spec`
   prints nothing; `grep -rc "console.log" libs/shared/auth/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v ":0"`
   prints nothing; and an e2e step after the sign-in reads every key of
   `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` and asserts that no value matches the
   JWT shape (three dot-separated base64url segments), which covers the
   client library's own stores as well as house code.

`libs/shared/auth/src/lib/session/transitions.ts` declares the transition
   table for the six states and `transitions.spec.ts` asserts every state and
   event pair (the spec iterates the table and the event list, so an
   unhandled pair fails); `npx nx test auth` exits 0.

Unit specs exist and pass for each matrix row: timeout on exchange,
   `invalid_grant`, expired-then-refresh-then-replay, refresh failure to
   sign-out, invalid signature, wrong audience, skew within and beyond
   tolerance, two concurrent `401`s producing one refresh request (asserted
   through the MSW handler's call count), `state` mismatch, redirect loop
   stop, cross-tab sign-out.

`core` exports `routePermissions` covering every `BasePaths` member
   (a spec asserts the record's keys equal the enum's values), guards use it,
   and `npx nx e2e dotln-e2e` includes: sign in through the mocked provider
   and land on `returnTo`; a denied route redirecting to `/denied`; an
   element hidden by `*dotlnHasPermission` for a user without the permission;
   token expiry during use followed by a transparent refresh; refresh failure
   returning to `/login`.

The production build contains no mock provider code:
   `npx nx build dotln --configuration=production` exits 0, and for the
   development signing key's identifier (the `kid` constant) and for every
   path the mocked provider's constants file declares (both listed in the
   evidence README), `grep -rl "<value>" dist/apps/dotln/browser` prints
   nothing; and the bearer token is attached only to requests under
   `apiBaseUrl` (a spec asserts a request to another origin carries no
   `Authorization` header).

`docs/dev-reference/security/authentication.md` states the storage rule,
   the refresh rule, the matrix, the provider swap and that the server
   enforces authorization while client checks shape presentation only
   (`grep -c "server enforces authorization" docs/dev-reference/security/authentication.md`
   is at least 1), and `docs/ai-reference/auth-rules.md` exists.

`node scripts/target-gate.mjs WO-008 --review` records a passing row for
   every declared command with no tracked-byte mutation, and
   `npm run test:docs` passes in the launchpad order worktree; the Preflight
   line ran before the first full gate.

goalReview.platformStandard:
the point is to create a platform, not to prove every
constructible case before filing, and the refutation pass must be made worth
its cost before a later pass pays it again.
goalReview.goalStandard:
## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the home
of the DotLn console, the Angular shell that will render DotLn's actor-board
view model. Its product purpose is a UI over DotLn's features, for playing
with them and changing them more intuitively, so that the Angular app improves
the platform, the platform the starter, the starter this fork, and the fork
the Angular app in turn. The operator means to live in that UI rather than in
terminals: an agent-orchestration view that shows status and lets them check
in on running sessions. The critical path runs from registering that repository in this
launchpad, through one witnessed target order that scaffolds the workspace, to a
foundation where a feature is added by convention: shared libraries, the
component taxonomy, events and stores, and a legitimate client-side
authentication and permission model. Later workstreams join the same way: one
registration and one planning pass each, with the fork's own machinery changes
cut as self orders beside them.

episode.statement: I was the plan refuter for the WO-012 pass, at base c0784de. I read the compiled prompt refute-prompt.json in full by parsing it with python3 -I and printing every section. As read-only evidence I read these files in the working tree (c0784de, clean): dotln.config.json, packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json, docs/repositories/dotln-angular.md and docs/workstreams/WS-001-dotln-angular.md. I also read excerpts of UPSTREAM.md and README.md at main and on chore/starter-update-v0.87.0, and KIT-MANIFEST.json at main, upstream/main and the update branch. Through git show and git grep at upstream/main and main, I read excerpts of scripts/lib/config.mjs, scripts/lib/contributions.mjs, scripts/worktree.mjs (publish), scripts/release.mjs (target release), scripts/lib/target-publish.mjs, scripts/lib/authority-grants.mjs, scripts/lib/target-worktree-close.mjs, scripts/work-orders.mjs, scripts/launchpad.mjs (verifyKit), scripts/lib/dependencies.mjs, scripts/lib/evidence-sources.mjs, scripts/test-target-worktree-release.mjs, scripts/kit/README.client.md and the package.json scripts. I counted grep matches in the generated docs/work-orders/README.md at main, c0784de and the update branch, and read the matching lines. I ran only read-only Git commands (rev-parse, status, branch, log, show, diff --stat, grep, merge-base, and cat-file --batch for a manifest hash comparison), plus python3 -I and shasum with output to stdout only. I compared commit author identities without printing them. I did not read docs/planning/*.md, docs/planning/refutations/, docs/lineage/idea-ledger.md, docs/intake/, docs/control/local/, any receipt, evidence or verification directory, docs/product/, or any work-order file. I ran no npm or node kit command, made no network call and used no model tool. I made no repository or Git write and spawned no agent. The harness refused one shell redirect and one Write of plan-result.json into the scratchpad (outside-project write with no equipped grant for role unknown, WO-144). I did not retry or bypass the refusal, I created neither deliverable file, and I returned both texts to the parent. Model: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), as my host system prompt reports. Reasoning effort: the host context shows a reasoning_effort value of 40; nothing else reports it.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No critical-path file is declared (goalReview.criticalPath is unavailable), so I used the route in the goal standard: registration, then a witnessed scaffold, then the foundation (shared libraries in WO-005, merged; component taxonomy in WO-006; events and stores in WO-007; auth in WO-008). WO-012 is a self order. Its critical-path value depends on update #14 merging. At upstream/main (v0.87.0), scripts/lib/contributions.mjs reads contributions.operatorAuthor from config, and 'Missing data grants no exemption'. That replaces the identity v0.85.0 hard-coded in main:scripts/lib/contributions.mjs. scripts/worktree.mjs:1231 runs contributionSignoffRules over origin/main..HEAD for every launchpad branch publish, whether a self order or target records, and sets exit code 1 before any push. On main I found 0 Signed-off-by trailers. All 42 non-merge commits on main, and the commits on the update branch, have one author identity, equal to the v0.85.0 hard-coded one (compared without printing it). So once #14 merges, the gate this order unblocks is the launchpad publish of WO-012 itself and of WO-006's records branch, and of every later order. NoOp after #14: every publish refuses at contribution-signoff, which is a hard stop on the critical path or a return to hand publication (WO-005 was already published by hand after a different kit refusal, a49161e). NoOp before #14: stay at v0.85.0, where the hard-coded exemption still passes; the cost is going without the v0.87.0 fields. Criterion 2's kit verification is upkeep, not a gate. I confirmed 977 files at e4c46109 in KIT-MANIFEST.json and UPSTREAM.md on upstream/main and on the update branch, and a read-only hash pass over the update-branch tree found 0 differing and 0 missing manifest files. The other parts unblock no gate inside this horizon. The display name has no consumer: WO-012's non-goals keep the Target release classification header off WO-006 to WO-008, and WS-001 defers it to the UI planning pass. The recorded NoOp is that no target Release exists, the state accepted since WO-011. The judge-only base policy has a recorded NoOp cost of zero (the profile says WO-005's close found no ignored file in the base checkout). Its cost is only prospective: 37,877 node_modules files reinstalled once the operator builds in the base checkout. The cost-table row for WO-012 has metrics null, so wall-clock, tokens and context bytes are unknown. That is not a hold.
orders.systemTraps: Of the five supplied trap rows, none has a worsening entry or reopenCandidate true, and none records a failure for WO-012. Policy resistance / fixes that fail (material): the order declares release.policy and moves release.close into allowedEffects. At v0.87.0, prepareTargetRelease (scripts/release.mjs:2523-2552) also needs exactly one **Target release classification:** header per order and an operator grant naming release.close in packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json (authorizeRegisteredEffects). The committed grant names only repo.push, pr.open and pr.thread.resolve, and its reason says tagging stays with the operator. Criterion 5 keeps that file out of the diff, and planning branches are refused writes outside docs/, so the guards cancel the intended release. The guard-refusal series (1, 3, 0, null) shows no current trend. Tragedy of the commons: about 80 KB of context and the full fixed cycle for about 300 bytes of config plus prose. Machinery share was 0.54 and 0.52 for the last two orders, and a config-only order is likely to push it back up. Tokens are unknown. Drift to low performance: cold-start bytes are flat at 29,364 and gate steps at 7. The risk is that a waiver becomes normal, because criterion 3 cannot pass as written; a CriterionWaived direction is already recorded once, on WO-004. Escalation: declaring the policy now makes every later DotLn-Angular order carry a header or have its close refused, and needs another self order for the grant. Process that creates more process. Success to the successful: the bundle takes the kit's newest fields. A cheaper alternative is not shown as considered: declare only contributions.operatorAuthor now, and declare the release policy, grant and first header together in the order that first releases. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the operatorAuthor part removes a recurring rescue (hand publication). The release part adds one, because its refusal appears only at WO-006's release close, after both pull requests merge, and recovery needs a self order or operator override:. Operator corrections were 0, 2, 1, with WO-005 unavailable. Rule beating: criterion 4's six thresholds already hold at the planning HEAD c0784de (1, 3, 1, 1, 5, 1), so it passes without the rewrite it is meant to evidence. Criterion 1's readback, by contrast, checks real values. Seeking the wrong goal: the identity declaration serves operator flow. The display name serves a release outcome that no order in this horizon produces.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line names no removal larger than the addition. It adds one release object, one baseDisposablePolicy key and one top-level contributions object to dotln.config.json (about 300 bytes). It also rewrites the profile's ## Release close section, adds WS-001 rows and adds evidence. The WS-001 rows are already present at the planning HEAD, where WO-012 appears 5 times. It says it 'Removes nothing tracked beyond the moved effect'. That one removal is release.close leaving deniedEffects, which widens the registration's authority rather than removing machinery. Stale profile text stays unless the executor removes it unprompted: 'The registration has no release key and continues to deny release.close' and 'Until WO-012 merges, the paragraphs below describe the registration as WO-011 left it'. No criterion checks that removal. In short, the order only adds. The addition is justified for contributions.operatorAuthor by a hard publish refusal after #14. It is not justified inside this horizon for the release declaration or the judge-only key.
orders.failureBehavior: Mostly not. Each mechanism refuses, keeping source and naming a remedy, instead of falling back to the old behavior. (1) contributions.operatorAuthor: if it is absent or does not match the author, worktree publish prints FAIL contribution-signoff and exits 1 before the push, and the v0.85.0 exemption does not come back. A malformed value refuses in loadConfig, which every config-reading command shares, so a typo stops the control plane until fixed. Criterion 1's exact readback guards against that. (2) Release policy: once the policy is declared, a header-less order throws at release close ('exactly one is needed') instead of falling back to no-release. An order with a header throws at authorizeRegisteredEffects while the operator grant is missing. Both appear only at release close, because worktree start and the gate do not check, so they come after the target and records pull requests have merged. No-release returns only if a self order removes the release key. (3) judge-only base policy: the base is still judged, and undeclared ignored material still refuses, as before. judge-only adds a refusal when retained output collides with fetched tracked paths, and it merges with --no-overwrite-ignore (scripts/lib/target-worktree-close.mjs:502-535 and 606-615). The remedy is to move the output or remove the key; delete is not an automatic fallback. Failure is loud and can be reversed through config, never silent. For (2), though, it lands at the costliest point.

findings.reason: As scoped, the release objective cannot complete. At v0.87.0, a declared target release needs an operator grant naming release.close in packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json. prepareTargetRelease calls authorizeRegisteredEffects, which needs a grant with grantedBy operator, repo dotln-angular, and release.close in both effects and operations. The kit's own fixture writes such a grant beside the profile change. The committed grant names only repo.push, pr.open and pr.thread.resolve, and records the operator direction of 2026-10-17 that tagging stays with the operator. Criterion 5 limits WO-012's diff to dotln.config.json, the README release claim, the order and docs/, and planning branches are refused writes outside docs/. So neither WO-012 nor the UI planning pass can add the grant. The first order with a header (WO-006, per WS-001) would refuse at release close: 'release.close require an admitted operator grant naming dotln-angular'. Repair: either bring the grant into WO-012's scope and criterion 5, with an operator decision that revisits the tagging direction, or leave release.policy undeclared until the order that adds the grant.
findings.reopenWhen: After WO-012 merges with grants.json unchanged, a release close or dry run for a dotln-angular order that carries a Target release classification header prints the release.close operator-grant refusal. Or WO-012's final diff is observed changing packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json to name release.close, which closes this finding.

findings.reason: The kit's semantics differ from the objective's wording. The objective says a target order that carries the header closes with a tag. Once release.policy is declared, the kit requires the header on every dotln-angular order: targetReleaseClassification throws 'release.policy is declared, but <order> carries no **Target release classification:** patch | minor | major header; exactly one is needed'. Release close calls it for every target order, with --publish or --dry-run. Nothing checks earlier, at worktree start or in the gate. WO-012's non-goals leave WO-006 to WO-008 without headers, and the compiled sequence has no step that adds them. WS-001 gives WO-006's header to the UI planning pass but says nothing for WO-007, WO-008 or later members. Each order without a header would merge both pull requests and then refuse at close.
findings.reopenWhen: After WO-012 merges, a dotln-angular order without exactly one **Target release classification:** header reaches release close, and the close prints 'exactly one is needed'. Or the sequence records a precondition that every dotln-angular member carries the header before activation, which closes this finding.

findings.reason: Criterion 3 cannot pass as written. The v0.87.0 index generator always emits 'Settled orders (closed, withdrawn, superseded and historical), ...', and index --check requires the README to equal that generated text. On the update branch, the docs/work-orders/README.md regenerated under v0.87.0 already gives grep -c -i 'historical' = 1. At the planning HEAD the count is 2, because WO-012's own card cites validateHistoricalWorkOrders. So 'index --check exits 0' and 'prints 0' cannot both hold unless a kit file is edited, which is a non-goal. The intended check, that no order is classed historical, needs a narrower pattern, such as the historical status cell or a Historical section heading.
findings.reopenWhen: At WO-012's final identity, npm run work-orders -- index --check exits 0 while grep -c -i 'historical' docs/work-orders/README.md prints more than 0, or criterion 3 is waived or edited during the order.

findings.reason: Criterion 4 already passes before the order runs. The planning HEAD c0784de must merge before WO-012 activates. There, docs/repositories/dotln-angular.md gives '^## Release close' = 1, 'DotLn Angular' = 3, 'judge-only' = 1 and 'node scripts/worktree.mjs publish' = 1. WS-001 gives 'WO-012' = 5 and 'docs/evidence/WO-012' = 1. So the evidence cannot show the promised rewrite. Nothing checks that the stale sentences are gone ('The registration has no release key and continues to deny release.close'; 'Until WO-012 merges, ...').
findings.reopenWhen: Criterion 4 is recorded as passing while the profile at WO-012's final identity still contains 'continues to deny' or 'Until WO-012 merges'.

findings.reason: judge-only is prospective risk reduction with no named blocked outcome. The profile records a NoOp cost of zero (WO-005's base checkout held no ignored file). The key also adds a new refusal: when untracked output in the base checkout collides with paths tracked in the fetched base, the close refuses with 'judge-only output collides with fetched tracked paths', and the base merge uses --no-overwrite-ignore. Under the default delete policy, the same files would have been removed first. The outcome it protects, the operator running the app from the base checkout, is not named in the subject.

Its gates are WO-005's merge, a planning pass that replaces the provisional base (WS-001: 'provisional; set when WO-005 merges', and the next planning pass sets the line and refutes the changed order), the starter `--draft` gate, and the operator's vendor confirmation (title: 'operator-confirmed vendor'; house rule 6 names PrimeNG (MIT); the profile defers the vendor and license check to this order). NoOp in the records: the row's metrics are null. NoOp leaves features without enforced roles.
orders.systemTraps: Escalation and tragedy of the commons (material, process): each provisional base (WO-006, WO-007, WO-008) needs its own planning pass and refutation after the predecessor merges, three more passes whose material change is one Repository line. The supplied platform standard says the refutation pass must be made worth its cost before a later pass pays it again, and the records already show two planning captures on 2026-10-18. Policy resistance: R1 ('lint refuses inject( under fragments/, templates/, composites/ and layouts/') and WS-001's taxonomy table ('Salesmen may inject platform tokens only (ElementRef, DOCUMENT)') disagree for fragments and templates. Criterion 2 follows R1 strictly (no inject or constructor at all), so a template that needs ElementRef or DOCUMENT for focus handling, which criterion 5's keyboard path may require, must move or carry an exception. Drift to low performance: lint:components joins the target's checks outside the declared gate, as in WO-005. Rule beating (low): criterion 1's vendor grep reads the package name from decisions.md, and R2 and R4 stay review-only by WS-001's own declaration. Shifting the burden: vendor confirmation is an operator decision at activation. Success to the successful: the vendor is a house rule, and the wrappers keep alternatives open. Seeking the wrong goal (none): the work is the product. Context is about 120 KB and 6 to 8 hours.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes the WO-004 placeholder page and adds three libraries, about 60 files, the vendor dependency, @axe-core/playwright, location lint overrides and the taxonomy documents. The additions are the deliverable; no process removal is named.
orders.failureBehavior: The vendor sits behind wrappers, so a vendor failure stays inside wrappers/ and can be swapped, which is a degradation route by design. The static-signal facade is the declared stand-in until WO-007. Location lint fails closed (R5): a misplaced file is a failure, not a warning, which is intended. If no vendor is confirmed at activation, no fallback is stated (for example house fragments without a vendor), and the order stalls on the operator.

orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance (material): msw is pinned to 3.x (`~3.0.3`, or the current 3.x) and criterion 4 requires `npm ls msw` to report 3.x, but no 2.x fallback is named. This session had no network, so whether 3.x is published was not verified. Drift to low performance: rule 16 hygiene exceptions are counted and printed, never refused, and no ceiling is recorded, so the count can only rise. Escalation: lint:hygiene and msw:init join the target's checks outside the declared gate, as in WO-005. Rule beating (low, well handled): criterion 4 proves the unhandled-request option by behavior, and criterion 5 proves the mocks and every handler path are absent from the production bundle. Tragedy of the commons: about 150 KB of context and 6 to 8 hours, the second-largest in the pass; tokens unknown. Success to the successful: ngrx-toolkit or a house withCallState stays open. Shifting the burden: none. Seeking the wrong goal: none.
orders.removalBalance: No, though it names a real removal: HomeFacade's static data, WO-006's stand-in. It adds four libraries, the MSW worker and handlers, interceptors, a hygiene script, about 70 files, three dependencies and two target commands.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades in development: the browser worker starts only when environment.mocks is true (criterion 4), so with mocks off, requests go through WO-005's proxy to /api, the prior behavior. In tests it deliberately refuses unhandled requests (criterion 4). If the toolkit's withCallState fails, the house implementation takes over (Cost line). The MSW 3.x pin is the one element with no degradation route.

findings.reason: The MSW major-version pin has no fallback. If 3.x is unavailable, or its worker API differs from the cited guides, criterion 4 cannot pass and the order refuses instead of degrading to the current 2.x line.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: The final foundation step ('a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model'). WS-001 is delivered when WO-004 to WO-008 merge, and this order unblocks the unfiled DotLn console feature the goal standard names as the product purpose. Its gates are WO-007's merge, the base-reset planning pass and the starter `--draft` gate. NoOp in the records: the row's metrics are null. NoOp leaves WS-001 undelivered.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (material): criterion 1's storage scan asserts that no stored value matches the JWT shape, so an opaque refresh or access token written to storage by the client library passes, and 'holds tokens only in memory' goes unproved for non-JWT tokens. The mock knows every token it issues and could assert that none appears in storage. The objective's 'swapping the mocked provider for a real one changes configuration and nothing in the Angular code' is documented (criterion 6) but no criterion exercises a second provider configuration. Policy resistance and secrets: the Cost line commits a development signing key to a public repository. A development key is not a credential to any real system, but it matches the private-key patterns forge secret scanning looks for: it can raise an alert and, where push protection covers the pattern, refuse the publish. Generating the key pair when the mock starts (jose) avoids committing it. Criterion 5 keeps the kid out of the production bundle but not out of the repository. Tragedy of the commons: the largest order (about 160 KB, 8 to 12 hours, 15 steps; tokens unknown), and the record shows 1 of the last 3 orders failed first verification (WO-003), so size raises re-verification exposure. Escalation, drift, success to the successful, shifting the burden and seeking the wrong goal are immaterial: no new commands, a stricter failure matrix, the client library is chosen at activation, no operator step is added, and the work is the product.
orders.removalBalance: No. It says 'Removes nothing' and adds libs/shared/auth with its kit, the mocked provider's handlers and key, two event groups, guards, a permission directive, two routes, about 60 files and two dependencies.
orders.failureBehavior: Fails toward safety by design: refresh failure and invalid tokens sign the user out, and a denied route redirects to /denied (criteria 3 and 4). Session loss on reload, from memory-only tokens, leads to a new sign-in through the provider rather than an error. The mock is excluded from production (criterion 5), and an unreachable real provider leads to /login. One failure refuses rather than degrades: committed private-key material can be refused by forge secret scanning when the branch is published.

findings.reason: The JWT-shape storage assertion misses opaque tokens, so a stored non-JWT refresh token passes. Comparing storage values with the tokens the mock issued would prove the memory-only rule.
findings.reopenWhen: The mocked provider or the chosen client library issues or stores a non-JWT token, or a storage value after sign-in equals a token the mock issued, while criterion 1's assertion passes.

findings.reason: The provider-swap property is stated in documentation but never exercised, so its evidence can pass without the behavior.

findings.reason: A committed development signing key puts private-key material in a public repository, where secret scanning can flag it or refuse the push. Generating the key when the mock starts removes the material.
findings.reopenWhen: After WO-008, a tracked DotLn-Angular file contains a PEM private-key block or a JWK with a private `d` member, or a secret-scanning alert or push refusal is raised on WO-008's branch.
